advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Constrain primary_endpoint_for's new second branch so it cannot return an endpoint from a slot other than the one whose (endpoint-applied) resolution matches `resolved`, avoiding a cross-slot endpoint leak for hosted Responses primaries.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:468: `if slot.endpoint and _resolve_target(slot.model, slot.provider, endpoint=None) == resolved:`
`_openai_target` returns `openai-responses:` when endpoint is None (model_classes.py:227), so an endpoint-carrying openai slot's endpoint=None resolution collides with a hosted slot's resolved target
Classes are consulted in CLASS_NAMES order (model_classes.py:462); an endpoint slot ordered before a matching hosted slot fires branch 2 first

Branch 1 already preserves the custom-endpoint openai-chat: case because an endpoint forces `openai-chat:` which matches the `openai-chat:` resolved string, so branch 2 is not needed for the intended _pai_model preservation path
advisory.finding: The new second branch in primary_endpoint_for can return a DIFFERENT slot's endpoint than the slot that produced `resolved`. For an OpenAI-family slot, `_resolve_target(slot.model, slot.provider, endpoint=None)` yields `openai-responses:<tail>`; if a hosted (endpoint-less) slot resolved to that same `openai-responses:<tail>` string, iterating an endpoint-carrying sibling slot first makes branch 2 match on the endpoint=None resolution and return that sibling's endpoint. The runner then folds it into cfg.base_url, misrouting a hosted-Responses primary through the custom-endpoint Chat builder.
scenarios: Two model-class slots both target gpt-4o: one hosted (no endpoint, resolves openai-responses:gpt-4o), one with a custom endpoint; the endpoint slot is earlier in CLASS_NAMES order
Runner resolves the hosted class, collapses to cfg.model=openai-responses:gpt-4o, then _recover_slot_endpoint calls primary_endpoint_for and gets the wrong slot's endpoint
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the second branch (branch 1 already matches the endpoint-forced openai-chat: case), or gate it so it only applies when `resolved` itself is an `openai-chat:` string, never an `openai-responses:` one.

advisory.finding: _normalize_transition_force rejects force=False with an error message that names force=True. Previously boolean force=False mapped to None (no bypass); now any bool including False raises, but the message misstates the offending value.
scenarios: A stale caller passing force=False (previously a no-op meaning 'do not force') now gets a TypeError whose text references force=True
advisory.suggested_fix: Word the message generically, e.g. 'boolean rebar.transition(force=...) was removed; use force="<explicit reason>"'.
